meta.title: The Story of the Widow Who Would Not Give Up
meta.verseText: Jesus told his disciples a story to show them that they should always pray and not give up. (Luke 18:1 NIrV)
meta.theme: God's kingdom grows when you pray and don't give up.

questions.text: Who told the story about the widow who would not give up?
questions.hint: He often taught with parables.
questions.explanation: Jesus told this parable to teach His followers that they should always pray and not give up.

questions.text: What is a person called when their husband has died?
questions.hint: It is the main character in today's story.
questions.explanation: A widow is a woman whose husband has died. In Jesus' time, this made life very hard because widows had little help.

questions.text: In the story, who did the widow keep going to for help?
questions.hint: This person decided if things were fair.
questions.explanation: The widow kept going to the judge again and again, asking him to help make things right for her.

questions.text: What is today's Bottom Line?
options: God's kingdom grows when you pray and don't give up.
Always tell the truth to your friends.
questions.hint: It's about praying and not quitting.
questions.explanation: The Bottom Line reminds us: God's kingdom grows when you pray and don't give up.

questions.text: The widow gave up quickly and stopped asking the judge for help.
questions.hint: The whole story is about NOT giving up.
questions.explanation: False. The widow did NOT give up. She kept coming back to the judge again and again until he helped her.

questions.text: Where is today's Bible story found?
questions.hint: It's in a Gospel that starts with the letter L.
questions.explanation: The story of the persistent widow is found in Luke 18:1-8.

questions.text: A story that Jesus told to teach a lesson is called a ______.
questions.hint: It starts with the letter P.
questions.explanation: A parable is a special story Jesus used to teach an important truth. The widow story is one of His parables.

questions.text: How did the judge treat the widow at first?
options: He ignored her and didn't care
questions.hint: He wasn't kind or caring at the start.
questions.explanation: At first the judge didn't care about helping her. He didn't listen or pay attention, but the widow kept coming back.

questions.text: What finally happened because the widow never gave up?
options: The judge decided to help her
She gave up and went home
questions.hint: Her not-giving-up paid off.
questions.explanation: Finally the judge decided to help her and made things right, because she never stopped asking.

questions.text: Why was life very hard for widows during the time Jesus lived?
options: They had to travel a lot
They had few ways to earn money or get help
They were not allowed to pray
questions.hint: Think about who could speak up for them.
questions.explanation: Widows had few ways to earn money or get help, and often no one to speak up for them when something unfair happened.

questions.text: What does the story teach us to do when we talk to God?
options: Keep praying and don't give up
questions.hint: Just like the widow kept asking.
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that we should always pray and not give up, just like the widow who kept asking.

questions.text: Jesus said if even an unfair judge helped the widow, how much more will God do?
options: Much more — He will help and answer us
questions.hint: God is far more loving than the judge.
questions.explanation: Jesus' point was that if an unfair judge finally helped, God—who loves us—will do even more when we pray to Him.

questions.text: God gets tired of hearing us pray and tells us to go away.
questions.hint: God always wants to hear from you.
questions.explanation: False. God never gets tired of you. He never says 'Go away' and never ignores you when you pray.

questions.text: What is God's kingdom?
options: A place far away we can never see
Anywhere that God is King and reigns
questions.hint: It's wherever God rules as King.
questions.explanation: God's kingdom is anywhere He reigns as King—where His love, faithfulness, truth, and goodness are the way things work.

questions.text: Keeping on praying helps our hearts stay ______ to God.
questions.hint: The opposite of far away.
questions.explanation: When we keep talking to God, it helps our hearts stay close to Him, even when things are slow or hard.

questions.text: Even when an answer to prayer is slow or hard, what is God doing?
questions.hint: He hears you every single time.
questions.explanation: Even when things are slow or hard, God is working and He is listening. He hears us every single time.

questions.text: Why did Jesus want His friends to notice the widow in the story?
options: To show how she kept trying even when it was hard
To show she was a judge
questions.hint: It's about her not quitting.
questions.explanation: Jesus wanted His friends to see how the widow kept trying even when things were hard, teaching us to keep praying.

questions.text: What grows when we pray and don't give up?
questions.hint: It's in the Bottom Line.
questions.explanation: God's kingdom grows when we pray and don't give up. God does great kingdom things when we keep talking to Him.

questions.text: What should you do this week when you have something hard you want to talk to God about?
options: Keep praying and don't give up
questions.hint: Be like the widow.
questions.explanation: The lesson challenges us to keep praying and praying about what we need this week and to not give up.

questions.text: If a friend is sick, what is a good way to be like the widow in the story?
options: Keep praying for your friend and don't give up
questions.hint: Persistent prayer!
questions.explanation: We can keep praying for the people we love, again and again, trusting God hears us every time.

questions.text: The best thing to do when a prayer hasn't been answered yet is to quit praying.
questions.hint: Remember the widow's example.
questions.explanation: False. Instead of quitting, we should keep praying and trust God, even when we have to wait.

questions.text: The opener asked kids to think of something they kept trying until they finally did it, like ______.
options: tying their shoes or riding a bike
questions.hint: Things that take practice.
questions.explanation: The lesson used examples like tying shoes, building a tall tower, or learning to ride a bike—things we keep trying until we succeed.

questions.text: How can you help God's kingdom grow, according to today's lesson?
options: By praying and not giving up
questions.hint: It matches the Bottom Line.
questions.explanation: We help God's kingdom grow by praying and not giving up, trusting God to do great kingdom things.

questions.text: When you feel scared of something, what does the lesson say you can do?
options: Keep praying to God about it
questions.hint: Bring it to God.
questions.explanation: The lesson invites us to talk to God about hard things—like being scared—and to keep praying and not give up.

questions.text: Trying something again and again, even when it's hard, shows that you are ______.
questions.hint: It's a good, encouraging word.
questions.explanation: The leader said trying something again and again shows how strong and brave you are.

questions.text: The parable teaches that we should always pray and not ______.
questions.hint: Two words: don't quit.
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1 says Jesus told the story to show that people should always pray and not give up.

questions.text: Which word describes the judge's attitude toward the widow at the start of the story?
questions.hint: He didn't listen or pay attention.
questions.explanation: The judge was uncaring at first—he didn't listen or pay attention, and he wasn't kind. Yet he still finally helped.

questions.text: What is the name of this summer's series the kids are on?
questions.hint: It's about God's kingdom and an adventure.
questions.explanation: The series is called 'Kingdom Quest—Living the Greatest Adventure,' all about living in God's kingdom.

questions.text: The widow needed help because someone was ______ her badly and she needed things made right.
questions.hint: Something unfair was happening to her.
questions.explanation: Someone was treating the widow badly, so she needed someone to speak up and make things right for her.

questions.text: God's kingdom is good because ______.
questions.hint: Think about who the King is.
questions.explanation: God's kingdom is good because the King is good. God is loving, joyful, kind, trustworthy, holy, and righteous.

questions.text: Prayer is one of the ways we stay connected to God and help His kingdom grow.
questions.hint: Remember the Bottom Line.
questions.explanation: True. Praying keeps our hearts close to God, and God's kingdom grows when we pray and don't give up.

questions.text: According to the lesson, how many times does God want us to talk to Him about what we need?
questions.hint: 'Talk to Him and talk to Him and talk to Him.'
questions.explanation: God wants us to talk to Him over and over again about what we want and need, and He never gets tired of us.

story.summary: Jesus told His followers a parable to teach them to always pray and never give up. In the story, a widow—a woman whose husband had died—had a big problem. Someone was treating her badly, and she needed help to make things right. She went to a judge, but the judge was uncaring. He didn't listen or pay attention. Still, the widow did not give up. She kept coming back to the judge again and again, asking for help. Finally, the judge decided to help her and made things right, all because she never quit asking. Jesus said that if even an unfair judge finally helped, then how much more will our loving God help us and answer when we pray! God never gets tired of us and always listens. So we should keep praying and not give up—because God's kingdom grows when we pray and don't give up.

scenes.title: The Widow's Big Problem
scenes.description: Jesus begins His parable by introducing a widow—a woman whose husband had died. Life was very hard for widows back then, because they had few ways to earn money or get help, and often no one to speak up for them. This widow was being treated badly and needed someone to make things right.

scenes.title: Going to the Uncaring Judge
scenes.description: The widow went to a judge to ask for help. But the judge didn't care about her. He didn't listen and he didn't pay attention. He was not kind or caring at all.

scenes.title: She Would Not Give Up
scenes.description: Even though the judge ignored her, the widow kept coming back again and again. She did not quit. She kept asking for help over and over, showing how strong and brave persistence can be.

scenes.title: The Judge Finally Helps
scenes.description: Because the widow never gave up, the judge finally decided to help her and made things right. Jesus explained that if even an unfair judge helped, our loving God will do even more when we pray and don't give up.

scenes.title: Keep Praying This Week
scenes.description: Jesus wants us to keep talking to God over and over about what we need. Praying keeps our hearts close to God, and even when answers are slow, God is working and listening. God's kingdom grows when we pray and don't give up.
